clue.text: Tips for sentence with unchanged opening word?

indicators.note: the tips of a word are its two ends, so the first and last letters of sentence are taken

parts.note: something unchanged stays the same

explanation.surface: A grammar question about how to end a sentence that keeps its first word the same.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tips for' takes SE, the outside letters of 'sentence'. The definition plays on 'Open sesame', the magic words that open the cave in Ali Baba.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Arabian Nights tale the password 'Open sesame' makes the robbers' cave door swing open.

clue.text: Buddhist scripture possibly drawing humanity heavenwards

indicators.note: in a down entry, going upwards reads the letters from bottom to top

parts.note: drawing is a form of art
us, all of us, stands for humanity

explanation.surface: A holy text might depict mankind rising up to heaven.
explanation.definitionFit: A sutra is a scriptural discourse in Buddhism; 'possibly' because sutras also belong to Hindu texts.

clue.text: Lacking date, one's rejected by Kelly and Irene heartlessly

indicators.note: rejected things are turned back, so these letters are read in reverse

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
the possessive S is kept as written
Ned Kelly, the Australian outlaw

indicators.note: without its heart, only the outer letters of the name remain

explanation.surface: Someone without a date is turned down by a couple named Kelly and Irene.
explanation.definitionFit: Sine die is Latin for 'without a day', used of a meeting adjourned with no date fixed.

clue.text: Host's scoffing a duck in eatery

indicators.note: to scoff is to eat greedily, taking something inside

parts.note: an MC is a master of ceremonies, a host, with the possessive S
Donald Duck, the Disney cartoon duck

explanation.surface: A host eats duck in a restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: McDonald's is the fast-food chain, a place to eat.

clue.text: Kate and Bill are people with intelligence

parts.note: Kate Moss, the British supermodel
a bill is an advertisement, AD for short

explanation.surface: Two named people, Kate and Bill, are said to be clever.
explanation.definitionFit: Mossad is Israel's national intelligence agency, a body of spies gathering secret information.

clue.text: Melancholy may follow this in ancient concert hall

definitions.meaning: Keats wrote the poem '... Melancholy', so the word Melancholy follows these words
a building for music in ancient Greece

explanation.surface: A sad feeling might follow a performance in an old auditorium.
explanation.definitionFit: Keats's poem title supplies the first sense; the Greek odeion, a roofed hall for musical contests, the second.

clue.text: Swordsman in bar sure to get drunk

indicators.note: drunk letters stagger out of order, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fencer in a pub is certain to end up drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A sabreur is a fighter or fencer who uses a sabre.

clue.text: Have to enter club nearer to the sea

indicators.note: one piece entering another goes inside it

parts.note: a driver is a golf club
to own is to have

explanation.surface: An instruction to join a club close to the coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Going downriver follows the flow towards the mouth, so downriver places are closer to the sea.

clue.text: Brain in head's spinning

indicators.note: something spinning turns round, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: nut is slang for the head
the S of the possessive is kept as it is

explanation.surface: A dizzy feeling: the brain inside one's head is spinning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brain' is a verb here, as in to brain someone with a blow to the head.
explanation.definitionFit: To brain someone is to hit them on the head, which would knock them senseless.

clue.text: Iffy salutations, welcoming king in formal attire

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: iffy means doubtful or risky, dicey
K is the chess abbreviation for king
bows are gestures of greeting

explanation.surface: Awkward greetings made while receiving a monarch in evening dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickey bows, or dicky bows, are the British informal name for bow ties worn with evening dress.

clue.text: Picture Spur Harry after his dream move?

definitions.text: Picture Spur Harry after his dream move?

parts.words: Picture Spur Harry after his dream move?
parts.note: Harry Kane, the England striker, played for Tottenham Hotspur (Spurs); imagine him after a transfer to Manchester City, and he becomes a City man, which names an Orson Welles film

explanation.surface: Imagine the Spurs footballer Harry once he had made his ideal transfer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picture' is both 'imagine' and the film itself; Spurs is the London club Tottenham Hotspur, Kane's old team.
explanation.definitionFit: Citizen Kane is Orson Welles's 1941 film, often called the greatest picture ever made.

clue.text: Peruvian perhaps fat, with a lot of weight to carry

parts.note: padding is extra fat on the body
a ton is a large unit of weight
to bear is to carry

explanation.surface: Someone from Peru, perhaps overweight, has a heavy load to carry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peruvian perhaps' misleads towards a person; the bear in the children's books came from 'darkest Peru'.
explanation.definitionFit: Paddington Bear, Michael Bond's marmalade-loving character, arrived in London from Peru, so he is an example of a Peruvian.

clue.text: Neither worse nor better, what's more

definitions.meaning: doing something ... is doing it equally well, no worse and no better

explanation.surface: A comparison that is neither worse nor better, added as an afterthought.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a comparison of equal quality and an adverb meaning also or besides.

clue.text: Cooks stocks along with recipe for famous courses

indicators.note: to stock is to hold, so one piece holds the others inside it

parts.note: stews means cooks slowly
and means along with
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin

explanation.surface: A chef simmers stock with a recipe for a celebrated set of dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'courses' are golf courses, not meal courses: St Andrews in Scotland is the home of golf.
explanation.definitionFit: St Andrews in Fife has the Old Course and other renowned golf links.

clue.text: Zero energy in computer storage device

parts.note: zip is informal for zero or nothing
drive is energy or vigour

explanation.surface: A storage gadget said to have no power inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A Zip drive was a 1990s removable disk drive for saving and moving computer files.

clue.text: Primitive human in games with two chess pieces

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school games
the king and a man, any chess piece, are two pieces

explanation.surface: An early hominid joins in games with some chessmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Peking Man is a fossil Homo erectus found near Beijing, an early human ancestor.

clue.text: Male cuts clothes, an Italian import

indicators.note: to clothe is to wrap around, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: pares means cuts or trims

explanation.surface: A man trims some garments, one of which came over from Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' is a verb here: PARES clothes M.
explanation.definitionFit: Parmesan is a hard cheese from the Parma region, brought into other countries from Italy.

clue.text: Partner of gangster from America caught a slug?

parts.note: a moll is a gangster's girlfriend
US is the United States
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A gangster's girlfriend from the States is caught taking a slug of drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slug' suggests a bullet or a swig; it is the shell-less creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A slug is a gastropod, belonging to the soft-bodied invertebrates of the phylum Mollusca.

clue.text: Greeting a group of men in Korean car

indicators.note: one piece sitting in another goes inside it, here before the car's last letter

parts.note: Kia is a South Korean car maker
OR is other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Saying hello to a crowd of men sitting in a Korean car.
explanation.walkthrough: OR, other ranks, is the crossword's usual group of men: soldiers who are not officers.
explanation.definitionFit: Kia ora is a Maori greeting used across New Zealand, meaning roughly be well.

clue.text: The price of a pint for one in Daisy's family

parts.note: a pint is typically a pint of ale
price means cost

explanation.surface: What a beer costs for a member of Daisy's household.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daisy's family' is the plant family Asteraceae, not a woman's relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Alecost, or costmary, is an aromatic herb of the daisy family once used to flavour beer.

clue.text: Indolence, after getting translated?

indicators.note: translating changes words into something new, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Idleness, rendered into another language, becomes a well-known phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: 'translated' is the anagram signal, and the Italian phrase is literally what indolence becomes in translation.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolce far niente is Italian for 'sweet doing nothing', pleasant idleness.

clue.text: Frame deceitful sort, getting beheaded

indicators.note: losing the head means losing the first letter

parts.note: a weasel is a sly, deceitful person

explanation.surface: Framing a cheat who is then executed.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a stand or frame that holds a painting.

clue.text: Count golf shot, without ball rising

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising reads the letters from bottom to top
without in the old sense of outside, so one piece is around the other

parts.note: a putt is a golf shot on the green
O is shaped like a ball

explanation.surface: Counting golf strokes, with the ball climbing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside: PUTT goes round O, and 'rising' turns PUTOT upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To tot up is to add up, a total count.

clue.text: Group of players put on outfits for speed

indicators.note: in a down-style build the team is placed onto the outfits, so it comes after them

parts.note: getups are outfits or costumes
a team is a group of players

explanation.surface: A sports team dresses in costumes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' looks like dressing up, but it only places the group of players after the outfits.
explanation.definitionFit: To get up steam is to gather speed, from steam engines building pressure; here a verb.

clue.text: German weaver denuded

indicators.note: stripped bare, so the outer letters are removed from the word

parts.note: Nick Bottom is the weaver in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream

explanation.surface: A weaver from Germany is left naked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German' is a noun: a man from Germany, as Otto is a typical German name.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto is a common German man's name, the setter's example of a German.

clue.text: One cuts two thirds of time off

indicators.note: keeping two thirds of a nine-letter phrase drops its final three letters

parts.note: sick leave is time off work when ill

explanation.surface: Someone takes most of a break from work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One cuts' looks like a person; it is a tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A sickle is a curved blade used to cut grain or grass.

clue.text: Like a march or an arch?

definitions.meaning: the arched middle of the foot

explanation.surface: A question comparing a march with an arch.
explanation.definitionFit: Marchers move in step together, and the instep is the raised arch of the foot.
